plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges to bid your true value minus a small increment. This is because any bid above your value risks winning at a loss. Bidding slightly below your value increases the chance of winning at a profit, while minimizing the risk of overpaying. Since this is round 1 and there is no history, I'll bid slightly below my value.

Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges to bid your value divided by 2, rounded to the nearest 0.1. This is because any bid above your value is irrational (you'd lose money if you win), and bidding significantly below your value risks losing to a slightly higher bid while potentially winning at a price you'd happily pay. My value is $29, so $29/2 = $14.5.

Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges to bid your value multiplied by 2/3. This is because any higher bid risks overpaying, and any lower bid risks letting someone else win an item you value highly. In this case, my value is $48. 2/3 of $48 is $32. Since bids are in $0.1 increments, I will bid $32.0.
